# Combat, actions and timing — provisional playtest integration

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the supplied combat/action/timing/vision scope.** [GPT's disposition](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FIRST_REVIEW.md) confirms the corrected candidate. This does not close all combat, movement, encounter or condition work. Original books, class cards and earlier drafts are preserved. The NEW decisions below apply to this candidate only.

Read alongside [core resolution and injury](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md), [conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md), [custom riders](CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md), [spell integration](SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md) and [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). This document explicitly supersedes conflicting provisional clauses only where listed. A specific reviewed feature retains its printed costs, prerequisites and exceptions.

## Source decisions

The [exact packet](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/COMBAT_ACTION_VISION_SOURCE_PACKET.json) contains 217 paragraphs from unchanged Core V2 and V6 books. Paragraph indices are zero-based all Word XML `w:p` descendants. [Source validation](COMBAT_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies quotations and whole-book hashes. The [first GPT proposal](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_ACTION_TIMING_FIRST_REVIEW.md), [counterexamples](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_COMBAT_COUNTEREXAMPLES.md) and [revised decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_COUNTEREXAMPLE_REVIEW.md) preserve the conference.

| Topic | Source / conflict | Candidate decision |
|---|---|---|
| Initiative, action list, encounter clock | Core 373–418 | Core controls; compatible V6 8066–8244 supplies detailed procedures. |
| Reaction | Core/V6 summarize one per round; V6 and class integration refresh own turn | NEW explicit interpretation: one resource between regular own-turn starts; no global-round reset. |
| Stances | Core 419–435; extra-turn ambiguity | Keep listed effects; NEW regular-turn selection and finite allowances. |
| Movement | Core 436–458; V6 mode switching subtracts physical distance | NEW spent-cost ledger prevents terrain/standing refunds; multiple legal Dashes each add Speed. |
| Maneuvers | Core 460–486 | Preserve sourced effects; NEW declaration, costs and endpoints fill missing execution details. |
| Grapple/Shove | V6 opposed procedure vs older shared-class generic DC | Ordinary maneuvers use V6 opposed rolls. Printed card saves/DCs retain their scope. |
| Prone and Invisible | Core/V6 conflicts already reviewed | Current condition reference controls, including Core ranged Prone disadvantage and Invisible position-reveal exception. |
| Round duration / simultaneous events | Sources do not give complete ordering | NEW preserved virtual markers and explicit start/end sequence below. |
| Ready | V6 casts and holds spell; generic Action or movement | Preserve that procedure; NEW one pending state and preparation/release details. |
| Hide/Search | Core lists actions; V6 unseen attacks | NEW passive DC and observer-specific Hidden procedure using Core task degrees. |
| Diagonals / terrain composition | 5-ft tile convention; missing full composition | NEW equal orthogonal/diagonal metric and additive movement costs. |
| Periodic and falling clocks | Existing reviewed overlays | Remain authoritative in their stated scope; no extra-turn tick or duplicated fall step. |
| Equipment, cargo and Sunder | Core delegates actual object/cargo systems | No invented durability, capacity or automatic cargo protection. These dependencies remain open. |

## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints. The helper excludes a specific current-end marker only if that marker would otherwise be selected: application during a turn at time1 with end3 excludes3 and selects9; application at/after3 also selects9, without erroneously skipping again to15.

At a regular turn's **start**, resolve in this order:

1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.

At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.

For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

Examples: dying at 0 rolls its death save before ordinary start-turn healing; a fatal death save is not undone by ordinary healing. Stable at 0 skips the save, then start-turn damage can break Stable. A natural 20 can restore 1 HP before a due Bleed drops it to 0 as a new drop event. If Decay expires while a Stable recovery deadline is already due, the old deadline resolves once without rerolling recovery time.

## Standard Actions

| Action | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Attack | Make the attacks legally granted by class and weapon. Replacing one attack does not replace the entire Action unless specified. |
| Cast | Use an Action-time spell or Resonance technique; all known/prepared, cost, component and target requirements apply. |
| Dash | Add one current Speed to each mode's turn cap; see movement ledger. Speed 0 grants none. A second legally paid Dash adds another Speed. |
| Disengage | Voluntary movement does not provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of that turn. |
| Dodge | Until next regular start, attacks from attackers you can see have disadvantage; your DEX saves have advantage. Benefit fails while Incapacitated or Speed 0. |
| Guard | +2 AC against the first attack against you before next regular start; consumed on that attack hit or miss. Guard state and Interpose permission remain until expiry even after the +2 is spent. |
| Aim | Action; no prior voluntary movement this turn, and no subsequent voluntary movement that turn. +2 to one ranged/spell attack before turn end. Forced movement does not cancel it. It grants no attack; a legal Bonus Action/extra Action/express attack must supply one. |
| Help | Advantage on a relevant ally check before next regular start, or assist an attack against a foe within 5 ft: the helped ally's first attack before that deadline has advantage. Assistance must be physically possible. |
| Hide / Search | Use the observer-specific procedures below. |
| Ready | Prepare an Action or movement; release uses Reaction as detailed below. |
| Use Object | Pay for the second ordinary interaction or an object's required Action activation. No extra hands/capacity are granted. |
| Improvise | Director declares ability, applicable proficiency, DC/opposed method and intended consequence before rolling. Success does not create unannounced conditions/actions. |

**Brace — NEW.** Action, choose one mode until next regular start. **Intercept:** choose a breach/doorway edge or current melee reach; when a hostile creature charges/leaps/breaches into it and enters legal reach, spend Reaction for one legal melee weapon attack after entry and before later movement/actions. **Hold Ground:** spend Reaction on the first applicable discrete push/pull/shove/knockback to reduce displacement 5 ft, minimum 0. It does not reduce damage, prevent independent Prone, stop gravity/fall steps, currents, conveyors, collapsing ground or teleportation, or grant support/hover. One Brace supplies one opportunity, not an extra Reaction.

**Rally — NEW.** Action; choose one ally within 30 ft able to perceive the rally and one active source-qualified Frightened record. CHA check at that record's source DC, otherwise 10; Success/Critical Success ends only that record. A later reviewed morale rule can supply a separate specific interaction. No automatic temporary HP, loyalty, belief or advantage.

**Withdraw.** Action; separate half-current-Speed movement budget, normal terrain costs, no opportunity attacks from that movement and +2 AC only while that movement resolves. Speed 0 grants none. Moving zero grants no lingering +2. Ordinary movement before/after remains separate. The separate budget is NEW interpretation of Core 480.

**Secure Cargo.** Core 482 preserves the wording “up to one Extraction Load class.” The subsequently reviewed [body and carrying guide](BODY_EQUIPMENT_PLAYTEST.md) supplies the provisional interpretation: spend an Action on one legal attach, lift, transfer or protective operation involving one actual cargo unit or physically constituted bundle with an assigned Extraction Class. Load measures burden; Extraction Class measures danger and logistics. Apply actual capacity, custody, hands, harnesses, checks and durability. The Action grants no extra capacity, equipment, automatic success, invulnerability or reduction in Extraction Class. Full equipment and extraction catalogs remain open.

## Ready

Spend an Action to declare a perceivable trigger and one legal Action-time action or movement. It expires next regular own-turn start. **NEW:** only one pending Ready per creature; replacing it loses the prior setup and any paid held-spell costs. No Bonus Action/Reaction ability, long ritual or multi-minute activity can be prepared by generic Ready.

The trigger happens first, then the readied response immediately follows before later events, unless a specific effect explicitly interrupts. On release spend the normal Reaction and recheck target, range, sight/perception, line of effect, ammunition and other prerequisites. An invalid or declined occurrence spends no release resource; the Ready can wait for another valid occurrence before expiry. This does not undo setup costs. Once released, it is consumed.

For ordinary nonspell actions, feature/ammunition costs are paid on release unless text charges setup. A readied **Attack Action** gets its legally available ordinary attack count; a feature limited to your own turn does not thereby work off-turn. Core Overwatch is explicitly one ranged attack, not that full Attack Action and not Soldier's distinct engine.

A readied spell is actually **cast at preparation**: choose spell/mode, verify legality, pay RP/material/other costs, provide components, resolve Dissonance/Refrain and cast-trigger effects once. Counterspell/cast-interruption opportunity occurs then, not again at release. Every held spell requires concentration, even ordinarily non-concentration spells; incompatible prior concentration ends. Lost concentration loses the held spell and costs. NEW: select the legal target/area point at release and recheck legality without repaying. At release the hold continues as ordinary spell concentration if required, otherwise ends after resolution. Expired/replaced/countered held spells do not refund paid costs.

Ready movement grants a separate current-Speed budget on release, pays terrain costs and can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. It grants no extra Action, Bonus Action or interaction.

Focused stance's Reaction restriction also blocks an ordinary Ready release; Ready does not create a Counterspell exception. Holding a spell does not waive any current Reaction prohibition.

**Spell-effect duration begins at release.** Its normal duration is anchored when the effect manifests, while Ready expiry and held concentration already run from preparation. A source explicitly tying a particular consequence to casting/preparation retains that consequence's stated clock. No casting cost, Refrain, Dissonance or cast trigger occurs a second time merely from release.

## Stances

Choose one stance during a **regular** own turn before the first event that would use any stance benefit/restriction: attack, spell, relevant check/save or movement. If none occurs, choose before turn end. No retroactive selection. It lasts until next regular start. NEW: extra turns preserve the stance and spent allowances; they cannot choose/replenish it.

| Stance | Effect |
|---|---|
| Aggressive | +2 damage once per qualifying weapon attack's damage packet; −2 AC. Not periodic or copied damage. |
| Guarded | +1 AC, advantage on explicit roll/contest resisting Shove, Speed −5 (minimum 0). Its +1 can coexist with Guard's first-attack +2, giving +3 then +1. This combination is explicitly allowed here. |
| Mobile | First 5 ft of actual voluntary movement does not provoke; no free movement is granted. Your opportunity attacks reduce each base weapon die one step: d12→d10→d8→d6→d4 (minimum d4). Rider dice unchanged. Die sequence is NEW. |
| Focused | Choose +1 save DC for one spell OR +1 to one attack roll from one spell. After use, no-Reaction-except-Counterspell restriction remains through expiry. This grants no Counterspell knowledge, free cost or extra Reaction. |
| Carrying | Choose one actual currently applicable cargo penalty to ignore; choice fixed through expiry. It does not increase capacity or erase all load limits. DEX saves have disadvantage. |

## Maneuvers and ordinary attacks

All opposed checks use Core total comparison: higher wins, exact tie preserves state. No natural-20 automatic victory or hidden task-degree effect on an opposed tie. A printed save-based class maneuver keeps its own method.

| Maneuver | Execution |
|---|---|
| Grapple | Replace one Attack Action attack; reach and target ≤one size larger. STR Athletics vs defender STR Athletics/DEX Acrobatics. Escape Action uses same opposed contest. NEW one free usable grasping hand/appendage per target; release freely on own turn. Ends if required reach breaks or grappler becomes Incapacitated. No concentration required. Dragging halves Speed unless target ≥two sizes smaller. Magical/card exceptions remain source-specific. |
| Shove | Replace one attack; same reach/size/contest limits; success pushes 5 ft away or knocks Prone. |
| Trip | Replace one melee attack, Athletics vs Athletics/Acrobatics, success Prone. NEW same one-size-larger cap. |
| Disarm | Replace one attack, Athletics or weapon check vs Athletics/Acrobatics. Item must be held and reachable. Attacker chooses legal adjacent unoccupied drop space, otherwise target's own space. Explicit non-droppable bonds prevent it; magic/curse alone does not. No severed attunement/ownership/curse. |
| Feint | Bonus Action Deception vs Insight; success advantage on next melee attack this turn only. |
| Sunder | Attack an object/shield/armor component/construct joint using its actual durability system rather than creature HP. Unspecified durability remains an equipment dependency. |
| Break Formation | Special Shove replacing one attack, same reach/size contest with attacker disadvantage. Success pushes 10 ft; snapshot target's adjacent allies before push and remove their Guard Action benefits. Does not remove Guarded stance or target's own Guard. |
| Overwatch | Ready one ranged attack against movement in a named lane. Reaction and ammunition paid at release. Distinct from Soldier's class engine. |

**Pin and Silence the Caster — NEW tradeoff.** Declare before rolling and take **−2 to that attack roll**. Each creature has one Pin token and one Silence the Caster token between starts of its regular turns. An unused token may be spent on any otherwise legal qualifying attack, including off-turn, extra-turn or readied attacks. A legal declaration followed by an attack roll consumes the token even on a miss; an illegal declaration rejected before rolling consumes nothing. Tokens refresh only at regular own-turn start, never on an extra turn or numbered-round boundary. One attack cannot combine another optional tactical maneuver. These provisional numbers require table playtesting.

Pin uses a ranged weapon attack. On hit deal ordinary damage and apply Speed −10 (floor 0), DC `8 + PB + attack ability modifier`. Ordinary Pins do not stack the penalty. At target's regular start, one optional STR Athletics task check against the highest active ordinary Pin DC ends all ordinary Pins on Success/Critical Success. Alternatively one Action removes all automatically. Source-specific card Pins do not silently acquire this generic definition or removal scope.

Silence the Caster uses a melee attack. On hit prevent verbal-component Reactions until target's next regular start. If concentrating, make exactly one CON concentration save at `max(10, floor(post-mitigation damage/2))`, including DC10 when damage is zero. This fulfills, rather than duplicates, the normal damage concentration check. It is not Core Silenced: speech and Action-time verbal casting remain possible.

**Interpose.** While Guarding, after an adjacent ally becomes an attack target but before its roll, spend Reaction and become target if legal for that attack (range/type/line/cover). NEW may move **up to** 5 ft using a separate terrain-paying budget, including zero if already legally positioned. Speed0 permits the zero-movement case only. It redirects one attack without cancelling or duplicating it. Guard's unspent +2 applies if this is the first attack against you. Voluntary movement has ordinary opportunity-attack consequences.

**Press.** On a melee hit during your regular turn, arm one target until next regular start. While unconsumed, another qualifying hit during that turn may replace it. If the target voluntarily retreats from an adjacent space, follow up to 5 ft into the vacated space using a separate terrain-paying budget; no Action/BA/Reaction. It can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. No following teleport/forced movement. Once used, cannot rearm before next regular turn, including during an extra turn. Speed0 prevents movement.

**Opportunity attack.** Spend Reaction for one melee attack against a seen hostile creature voluntarily leaving reach, immediately **before** exit. Forced movement/teleport do not trigger; Disengage suppresses it for its stated turn. Specific reviewed triggers may override these conditions.

**Two-weapon fighting.** After taking Attack and attacking with a Light melee weapon in one hand, spend Bonus Action for one attack with a different Light melee weapon in the other hand. Do not add a positive ability modifier to that attack's damage; include a negative modifier. This grants neither another Bonus Action nor a class feature.

## Movement and geometry

Track **spent movement cost**, not distance, for ordinary turn movement. Mode cap = `(1 + number of legal Dash actions this turn) × current Speed for that mode`; remaining = max(0, cap − spent cost). Switching modes never refunds cost. Recalculate cap on Speed changes, preserving spent cost. Stand from Prone costs floor(half current Speed) and requires nonzero Speed and enough budget. Dropping Prone costs no movement.

For each foot traveled, normal/difficult/severe terrain costs 1/2/3; use strongest terrain only. Add +1 for crawling and +1 for squeezing. Crawl in difficult =3:1; crawl+squeeze in difficult =4:1. A nonhostile occupied space counts as difficult terrain. Enter a hostile creature's space only with ≥two-size difference or an express feature; never willingly end in an occupied space. Squeeze through a space one size smaller, with own attack/DEX-save disadvantage and attacks-against advantage.

Walk10 through difficult spends20; switch to Fly30 leaves10. Stand with Speed30 spends15; switching to Fly30 leaves15. Two legal Dashes at Speed30 give cap90; prior expenditure still counts. Interpose/Press grant5 budget: they cannot enter a difficult 5-ft tile costing10. Their separate budgets never refill ordinary movement. Ready movement uses Speed at release; Withdraw uses half current Speed. All voluntary movement requires nonzero relevant Speed.

Forced movement does not use these ledgers or provoke ordinary opportunity attacks, cannot place creatures in solid matter, and stops at obstacles. Teleport does not traverse intervening terrain or spend Speed unless printed; it requires a legal destination. Speed0 alone does not block forced movement or teleport. Flight with Prone/Speed0/lost support causes Falling unless Hover or an explicit magical support exception applies; use the existing fixed Fall Marker procedure. Reaching support ends Falling.

NEW grid metric: each orthogonal or diagonal neighboring tile is 5 ft; use the same metric for ordinary ranges/areas. No diagonal cut through a corner when both adjacent orthogonal sides are completely blocked. Exact templates, 3D geometry, mounts, chases, jumping, climbing/swimming procedures and currents need further source review.

## Cover, sight, Hide and Search

Keep **visibility**, **known location**, and **line of effect** separate. Seeing through a barrier does not itself permit attacking through it. Best cover only: half +2 AC/DEX saves; three-quarters +5; total prevents direct targeting through that obstruction. Never add +2 and +5. For areas, evaluate line/cover from the area's origin to each target; total cover there excludes a creature unless the effect explicitly travels around/through the obstruction. The origin point itself must be legally targetable.

Within normal ranged range, no range penalty; beyond normal through long, disadvantage; beyond long, illegal. Ranged attacks also have disadvantage when within5ft of a non-Incapacitated hostile that can see the attacker, even if the attacker cannot see that hostile. All advantage/disadvantage follows the single cancellation rule.

NEW **Hide**: permitted only against observers unable to see you clearly or where a feature permits. Roll DEX Stealth once, record natural die and total. Against each observer's passive DC `10 + WIS Perception modifier including applicable proficiency`, use the Core four-degree task system. Meet DC succeeds before natural1/20 degree adjustment; Success/Critical Success establishes Hidden for that observer. No unsourced passive ±5 adjustment for advantage/disadvantage. Actual Search rolls use their normal modifiers.

Hidden means that observer cannot see you and does not know your location. Clear sight or learning your position ends Hidden for that observer. Moving between hiding places can retain Hidden only if no clear sight/revealing event occurs. A failed Hide cannot simply be rerolled unchanged; a materially new hiding position, concealment, distraction, sight-breaking event or express reroll feature is required. Hidden is not a generic immunity or a free stealth roll for every move.

**Search** Action: WIS Perception for sensory detection; INT Investigation for appropriate traces/deduction; Core Arcana/Engineering where relevant. Directly locating a Hidden creature defaults to Perception against its recorded final Stealth total as a static DC, using task degrees/natural shifts. Success reveals location only to the searcher and ends Hidden for that observer, without automatically granting sight. Communicate normally to inform others. Search can be repeated on later turns by paying the Action.

Attacks against unseen targets have disadvantage; unseen attackers have advantage, subject to the **Core Invisible exception**: once its position is known, Invisible's own attack modifiers end for that observer and cannot immediately return solely because it remains Invisible. Independent darkness, smoke, blindness or hiding can still supply modifiers.

Resolve an attack using pre-attack information; afterward reveal location to observers able to perceive its evidence. If an unseen target's location is unknown, do not directly choose it for a creature-target effect. A weapon/projectile can instead attack a suspected space: wrong space automatically misses; correct space uses unseen rules. A “creature you can see” requirement is never met by position knowledge alone. Area effects can target legal points under their own rules.

## Scope and validation

[Reference checks](COMBAT_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) exercise selected budgets, clocks and edge cases. They do not implement map visibility, inventory, feature legality, complete event dispatch, all maneuvers or a live application. No claim of encounter balance or human playtest completion follows from a passing report.

`start_life_sequence` receives already-resolved/arbitrated HP events; it does not perform condition-family arbitration, cure processing, trigger generation, duration expiry, target legality, defense calculations or general simultaneous-event dispatch. `hide_results` answers only whether Hidden is established, collapsing the two success degrees and two failure degrees; it does not retain the full task-degree record. The Reaction helper models the ordinary resource, not additional Reaction grants printed on specific cards.

Remaining work includes cargo terminology/capacity/durability; detailed movement/environment/chases; area templates and sensory abilities; summons/boss full-turn examples; all-source class/spell semantic interactions and specific resource grants; and the whole-game ledger's other acceptance gates.

## Resolve the kind of protection first

Guardian Pulse changes the target of an attack before comparing its original roll with AC. The Guardian becomes the actual hit/miss and on-hit-rider target. One attack can be retargeted once. Multiple offers are chosen by the original intended target; only the selected Guardian spends its Reaction/use. After the incoming attack fully resolves, a surviving, eligible Guardian may make the printed counterattack against an attacker in reach whether the original attack hit or missed. This free attack cannot grant another free attack or Action. Retargeting does not spend the later damage-transfer opportunity.

Bloodbond and Veinlock Tether divide the finalized raw damage before either recipient's mitigation. Attack/save success, save-halving and critical dice have already determined that amount. Bloodbond transfers one quarter, rounded down; Veinlock instead chooses up to S+M. Each recipient applies its own eligible defenses once to its own share.

Other supplied damage transfers divide damage after the original target's defenses and legal pure prevention, before temporary HP. Their transferred portions keep damage type and skip another DR/resistance/immunity/prevention stage. Temporary HP, applicable HP floors, would-die replacements, Wounds, concentration and ordinary life consequences still apply. “Unmitigated damage” does not mean “death cannot be prevented.”

Pure prevention removes damage without creating a second recipient. Elemental Absorption adds its resistance during ordinary defenses. Aura of Bonds and Crown reductions use the strongest applicable class flat reduction, then resistance/immunity. Finite/reactive prevention such as Bloom and Ancestral Guardian follows those defenses before post-defense transfer and temporary HP. Verify additional item/spell sources before treating this as universal defense ordering.

Redirecting Palm prevents half the Monk's post-defense damage, rounded down. The Monk keeps the remainder. A second enemy distinct from the triggering melee attacker, within5feet, can receive new force damage equal to the prevented amount, capped at Monk level. That new damage gets its own defenses; it is not a transferred attack or critical hit. With no second enemy, the Monk still receives the reduction.

Direct HP payments from Blood Sacrifice, Flesh-to-RP, Profane Exchange and Channel Life stay outside the damage sequence. They bypass temporary HP, obey their own legal minimum HP and do not create damage/Wound/resource triggers from paying the cost. Healing-recipient substitution and excess-healing conversion also remain distinct operations.

## One transfer operation and exact amounts

A root here means one original recipient's damage packet. A shared area cast has a separate root for each original recipient, under the same cast/roll identity.

One such root accepts one damage-sharing operation across all owners. A pre-mitigation split locks both its retained original portion and transferred portions against later transfer. Burden Shared can divide one operation among up to two other explicitly willing recipients. It does not create two redirection events. No transferred recipient may be the original damage target.

**New stage-precedence integration:** consider pre-mitigation offers before applying defenses, and post-defense offers afterward. Within the same stage, select eligible positive mandatory/automatic protection before optional offers; competing mandatory claims are chosen by the original damage target. A legally chosen Bloodbond/Veinlock operation can therefore preempt later Aegis/Final Stand because that root is already claimed. Do not preview or consume defenses/Bloom to decide a later-stage preference. The helper accepts an already selected legal operation; it does not select Reactions or schedule automatic offers.

Optional transfer requires a positive chosen amount and available damage. Zero transfer cannot spend an optional Reaction/resource/use. A mandatory rounded-zero share does nothing and spends no transfer allowance. An independently legal prevention component can still occur.

| Source | Transferred amount |
|---|---|
| Bloodbond | floor(raw damage/4), fixed |
| Veinlock Tether / Shared Breath / Selfless Guardian | chosen up to S+M |
| Protective Stance / Emergency Protocols | min(S+M, available damage), fixed |
| Life Linked | chosen up to floor(available damage/2) |
| Guardian Tissue | floor(available damage/3), fixed |
| Aegis Incarnate / Martyr's Share | floor(available damage/2), fixed |

| Aura of the Crown | chosen up to M |
| Crown of Embers / Burden Shared | chosen up to level+M |
| Crown Undying | chosen up to remaining level+M round allowance |
| Final Stand | all available damage, subject to shared allowance |

## Hit identity and final damage accounting

The original damage target retains its original hit, failed-save, critical and on-hit-rider identity even if all damage is transferred. A rider that requires positive damage must recheck the actual remaining packet. A transferred recipient was not hit by that attack and did not fail its save; it receives no attached poison/control/maiming/knockout rider merely because damage moved.

Accordingly, transferred damage from a critical attack gives an already0HP recipient the ordinary one damage failure, not two critical-hit failures. Concentration still sees the transferred recipient's resolved packet even if temporary HP absorbs all of it.

Use the [reviewed life-state interface](HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md) after resolving each final recipient. Numeric actual damage is temporary HP absorbed plus actual normal HP lost, excluding overkill and damage prevented by an HP floor. Sum each terminal recipient once. Do not also count the unsplit parent or unrelated counterdamage.

Physical root totals include every recipient. A healing/resource/reflection consumer sums only branches permitted for that consumer and qualifying for its own source's target predicate. For example, a meaningful-hostile-only drain does not automatically count damage transferred onto a friendly protector. Check all applicable flags for a compound trigger, such as a passive healing proc.

## Shared handling

This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications.

Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Gain a level

Opening campaigns officially use milestones. The Director’s announced milestones grant advancement; a CR-to-XP UI helper is not the official Opening reward law. The book’s cumulative XP thresholds remain available for tables using optional XP. See [XP provenance](XP_ADVANCEMENT_CANON.md).

Each earned advancement adds one total character level, to a combined maximum of 20. Choose one existing Base class to advance, or enter one new Base class if eligible. Process multiple earned levels one at a time; do not skip intervening choices.

1. Record the gained class and new class level. Recalculate total level and PB: +2 at total 1–4, +3 at 5–8, +4 at 9–12, +5 at 13–16, +6 at 17–20.
2. Add one new unspent Hit Die of the gained class’s size. Previously spent Hit Dice remain spent; gaining this die does not refresh any earlier die. For HP, roll that die or use its fixed rounded-up average: d6→4, d8→5, d10→6, d12→7. Record the base result before CON. This includes taking a new class’s first level after character level 1; maximum first-level HP is never granted again.
3. Apply exactly the gained class’s acquisition row, automatic improvements and class-level prerequisites. Complete its choices and any newly reached Arch/Hero gate. Automatic grants, scheduled selections and ASIs are distinct; do not pay a selection twice or grant an extra selection because the same feature appears in a legacy table.
4. At an ASI milestone, increase one score by 2 or two scores by 1, normally no higher than 20, or select one eligible operational feat. Ordinary milestones are class levels 4/8/12/16/19; Oracle uses 4/8/14/19. Follow any already-reviewed specific exception. No starting feat or repeatable feat is implied. [Eight complete feat options](FEAT_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md) do not make the other 327 complete.
5. Update legal repertoire, prepared capacity, class scaling and resource maxima at the gained **class** level. Use class-specific Druid preparation, Wizard spellbook/matrices and other explicit rules before generic acquisition defaults. New capacity does not provide an unnamed spell, an unearned choice, a filled Echo record or an extra prepared spell without the required preparation procedure.
6. Recompute base maximum HP from all attained-level records using current CON: sum(max(1, each stored base value + current CON modifier)). Then apply the separate [maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md), including compatible bonuses, reductions and systemic factors. Do not feed an already modified maximum back in as the base.
7. Keep current HP and spent resources unchanged except for a downward clamp when a maximum falls. An ordinary level-up is not healing or a rest: it cannot revive a downed/dead character, erase Wounds or refill already spent Hit Dice, RP, RC, class pools, item charges or uses. Newly granted features still follow an explicit acquisition/initialization clause if they have one; “gain a maximum” alone does not mean “restore current.”

**New HP completion:** each level’s HP contribution has a minimum of 1. Recompute those individual floors after permanent CON changes. This preserves retroactive CON adjustment without a naive level×modifier-change formula that can bypass a floor. Capacity increases grant no current HP; decreases can clamp current HP without damage/healing triggers, consistent with the reviewed maximum-HP interface. Temporary ability effects follow their own actual source rules rather than being silently treated as permanent advancement.

## One shared RP pool

Calculate each eligible class’s own current candidate RP pool at its own class level. Sort these classes by:

1. Caster tier: Full (Cleric, Druid, Mage, Wizard), then Half (Paladin, Ranger), then Hybrid (Bard, Shaman, Mirrorsage, Crimson Agent), then Minor (Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker).
2. Within a tier, higher class level first.
3. If class levels tie, higher actual RP pool first.
4. If both tie, the class acquired earlier first. Record that order; do not choose a different primary per cast.

Oracle, Soldier and Warrior contribute no RP pool. Maximum RP = the first class’s full pool + ceil(one quarter of the second class’s pool). With only one eligible class use its pool; with none, maximum RP is 0. Third and later eligible classes contribute no extra capacity, while retaining their earned class features and legal repertoire. Use current Core V2 candidate pools, not the older smaller companion-derived tables.

All RP-paid spells and techniques use this one merged pool unless an exact rule names another resource. RC, BG, Momentum, Ki, Conviction, Lay on Hands and other class resources remain separate. A change in the primary class or maximum is not recovery: preserve current RP and clamp only if above the new maximum. This can reduce maximum RP when a newly entered higher-tier class becomes primary; do not silently choose a larger lower-tier pool instead.

Each ordinary cast declares its casting class before costs. That class must independently know/prepare the spell, meet its school/rank gate and supply its own casting ability. Another class’s levels or repertoire cannot fill those requirements. Where two classes know the same spell, choosing its casting class does not create a second spell identity.

## Armor and shields

Choose one applicable AC formula. Light armor adds the full DEX modifier to its printed base. Medium adds `min(DEX modifier, 2)`, including a negative modifier. Heavy uses its fixed AC without positive or negative DEX. Explicit separate AC bonuses apply only when their own requirements are met.

One usable equipped shield contributes its printed bonus: buckler +1, shield +2, tower shield +3. No second shield bonus. Elven weave's printed Stealth advantage uses ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Dwarven plate is AC 18; its descriptive superior protection adds nothing. Scale mail's description adds no slashing resistance. Tower shield adds no unprinted cover or additional movement penalty.

**Nonproficient worn armor.** Retain V6 disadvantage on STR/DEX ability checks, saving throws and attacks. Core replaces the older casting prohibition: spells remain permitted, but an RP-priced spell costs +1 RP once per cast and concentration checks/saves have disadvantage. Multiple nonproficient armor pieces never multiply this surcharge. A normal 0-RP spell using the RP price interface can cost 1 RP. Apply this ordinary price addition before the already reviewed eligible reductions and final Resonance Influence step.

**Nonproficient shield — new completion.** While using a shield without shield proficiency, apply the STR/DEX check/save/attack disadvantage. A shield alone adds neither Core's armor RP surcharge nor concentration disadvantage and does not prohibit casting. Core names worn armor for those casting penalties.

A charge-only ancestry spell, Oracle effect or other cast with no RP-price interface acquires no RP price or pool from nonproficient armor. Actual concentration still has disadvantage from nonproficient worn armor. Hands, spell components and other independent casting restrictions remain.

**Strength minimum — new completion.** If one or more equipped armor/shield records have a listed STR minimum you do not meet, reduce Speed by 10 feet total, minimum 0. This is not a minimum to equip; multiple deficient pieces do not stack the reduction. This penalty can coexist with Load/Burden.

The Dwarf's printed rule that Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor prevents this penalty when the deficient item is heavy armor. It does not waive Load/Burden, another movement penalty or a tower shield's separate STR minimum. If a table chooses V6's preserved optional encumbrance alternate, that alternate ignores the Armor Table Strength column; the active reviewed Load procedure is not that alternate.

| Equipment | Don | Doff |
|---|---|---|
| Light armor | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| Medium armor | 5 minutes | 1 minute |
| Heavy armor | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| Any shield | 1 Action | 1 Action |

One actual assisting creature halves doff time only; a shield still takes at least one Action. Additional helpers do not repeatedly halve it.

## Hands and focuses

A buckler straps to one forearm. Its partially available hand can carry a small nonweapon object, but supplies no free S hand, loading hand, second-weapon attack, two-handed weapon support or active focus manipulation. An ordinary shield or tower shield occupies one hand. Soldier Shield Trained is a specific selected-feature exception for its repeating-crossbow/strapped-shield use, with that feature's actual reload requirements.

A two-handed weapon requires both hands when attacking with it. Releasing one grip costs no Action; regripping is part of its next legal use. This does not free a hand already occupied by another object, restraint or incompatible anatomy.

F requires an actual focus legal for the casting source. A hand holding only that focus may manipulate it and supply S for the same cast; the focus itself is not a conflicting object. A weapon, shield, second object, loading requirement or other hand restriction can make that hand unavailable. An item independently serving as both weapon and focus can use this rule only when an actual source authorizes that item as the caster's focus.

A holy symbol may supply F while held, visibly worn or borne on a shield where that casting source permits holy symbols. A worn or shield-borne symbol does not supply a free S hand. V still requires actual audible speech, and neither a focus nor component pouch waives explicitly priced or consumed materials. The component pouch supplies its ordinary storage function; this guide does not give it a new universal F substitution.

The following focus assignments are **new class integration** for actual legal class spells requiring F. They grant no spells or resource pools. Exact class features may override their own focus rules.

| Bard | One actual instrument |
| Cleric, Paladin | Holy symbol |

## Weapons and ammunition

Use the source table's exact weapon damage, type, properties, cost and weight. Proficiency follows the reviewed [character foundation](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md), not the source introduction's general statement about most people using simple weapons. A normal proficient attack adds PB once. Normal ability damage follows the attack's actual rules; an item procedure saying no ability damage overrides it for that item.

- **Finesse:** choose STR or DEX for both attack and damage.
- **Thrown:** a thrown melee weapon uses its ordinary melee ability; Finesse can still supply its choice.
- **Heavy:** Small creatures attack with disadvantage. Extending this to Tiny is a new completion.
- **Light:** enables only the actual reviewed Two-Weapon Fighting procedure, not an independent free attack.
- **Reach:** add 5 feet for that weapon's attacks and its actual opportunity-attack reach.
- **Two-handed:** both hands are required for an attack, subject to an explicit feature exception.
- **Versatile:** use the printed alternate damage for an actual two-handed melee attack.
- **Ammunition:** spend one real compatible ammunition unit per attack. Drawing it is part of the attack; non-repeating loading needs an available hand. Using an ammunition weapon in melee is improvised; a sling must be loaded to deal its improvised damage.
- **Loading:** only one ammunition attack per Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, regardless of Extra Attack. This is not one attack per entire turn or round.
- **Range:** the first number is normal range, the second maximum. Beyond normal range gives disadvantage; beyond maximum is illegal. Ordinary close-range ranged-attack rules still apply.

After an encounter, one uninterrupted minute searching accessible locations recovers `floor(eligible ordinary ammunition expended in that encounter / 2)`. Resolve recovery once for that encounter's expended ammunition; another search cannot recover another half. Only physically accessible, intact ordinary ammunition qualifies. Destroyed, consumed, irretrievable or specifically nonrecoverable ammunition does not. Recovered units remain the same physical items and cannot exist in two inventories. Nets and ordinary thrown weapons do not use this half-ammunition rule.

**Ammunition retail units.** A source ammunition bundle remains the ordinary market purchase unit. `unitPriceCp` and `unitWeightLb` are derived inventory/accounting values and do not by themselves guarantee that a merchant sells fractional bundles. If an actual buyer or seller agrees to split a bundle, price the agreed quantity proportionally and apply transaction rounding once to the final transaction. Starting-kit references record one retail bundle and its twenty `grantedUnits`, not twenty bundles.

**Lance.** Attacks against a target within 5 feet have disadvantage. It requires two hands unless mounted; the item supplies no mount or general mounted-combat procedure.

**Net.** A hit restrains a Large-or-smaller creature unless formless; it deals no damage. Its range remains 5/15 feet. The target or a helper within reach can spend an Action on DC 10 STR to free it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net against AC 10 destroys it and frees the victim without hurting that victim. When using a net with an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, make only one attack for that Action/BA/Reaction regardless of normal attack count. Use the reviewed Restrained condition. A missed net remains an actual object at the target location if physically accessible, not an automatically returned weapon.

**Improvised weapon.** Before rolling, the Director may agree that an actual similar object uses an existing weapon's full profile and relevant proficiency. Otherwise it deals 1d4 appropriate physical damage, with no PB absent actual improvised-weapon proficiency. Throwing an object without Thrown, or using a ranged weapon in melee, uses the improvised rule; improvised throwing range is 20/60 feet.

**Silvering.** Silver one weapon or ten ammunition units for 100 gp. This supplies actual silver eligibility only, with no automatic magic tag, attack bonus or damage bonus.

### New class equipment profiles

| Item | Price | Weight | Profile |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Repeating heavy crossbow | 100 gp | 20 lb | Martial ranged; 1d10 piercing; 80/320 feet; Heavy, Two-handed, Ammunition, Repeating 5 |
| Kama | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 slashing; Light |
| Nunchaku | 2 gp | 2 lb | Simple melee; 1d4 bludgeoning; Light |

**Repeating 5:** an internal magazine holds five bolts, replaces Loading, and spends one bolt per attack. An Action with an appropriate free loading hand loads up to five actually carried bolts. No spare-magazine multiplication, free refill or sixth shot. An exact feature such as Tactical Reload can change the action cost without creating ammunition. The ordinary heavy crossbow remains its separate source profile: 50 gp, 18 lb, 1d10 piercing, 100/400 feet and Loading.

The new **Sidearm** tag applies only to dagger, club, light hammer, handaxe and hand crossbow. Soldier's actual sidearm proficiency can therefore use those profiles; the tag supplies no new statistics or general Martial proficiency. Monk/Shaman staff maps to quarterstaff. Symbolic or relic weapons need an actual existing profile. Kama and nunchaku are not automatically Finesse.

## Equipment grade

An explicit V6 equipment grade changes the item's statistics and mundane baseline price as below. Structural damage does not automatically change grade. Ordinary grade does not create magical eligibility. Only one equipment grade applies.

| Grade | Worn armor | Weapon | Baseline price |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Crude | −1 AC; half normal structural HP, rounded down, minimum 1 | −1 attack; natural-1 break check | ×0.5, new price completion |
| Standard | Printed profile | Printed profile | ×1 |
| Fine | +1 AC | +1 attack | ×3 |
| Superior | +2 AC; 80% ordinary weight | +2 attack; one extra single base weapon die on a critical | ×10 |
| Exceptional | +3 AC; 70% ordinary weight | +3 attack; two extra single base weapon dice on a critical | ×25 |

Armor grade applies to worn suits, not shield AC. A future explicit crafted output may define its own shield improvements. Weapons gain no generic flat damage bonus. On a critical, double the ordinary damage dice, then add the quality dice once; a greatsword's extra quality die is one d6, not its entire 2d6 profile. A Crude weapon's natural-1 attack rolls d100: 5 or less sets structural HP to zero and breaks it. Its material remains recoverable.

Exceptional's source “minor special property” provides no additional effect until an exact property is authored. No free random enchantment is implied. Repair preserves the surviving item's recorded grade unless an exact procedure changes it.

Keep three distinct records:

| Record | What it affects |

| V6 equipment grade | The above combat statistics and mundane baseline price |
| Crafting outcome such as Exceptional or Masterwork | That recipe's actual yield, charges, catalyst or result procedure |
| Core artifact-market Quality | One factor inside the actual artifact valuation formula |

A successful craft does not automatically acquire a V6 grade. A recipe must explicitly specify its resulting equipment grade. ## Lifeleech — Magic; actual spellcasting ability

Before your spell's damage resolves, designate one eligible hostile target for that spell root and canonical round/window. Your first positive actual necrotic damage to that target in the window commits the entitlement, even if the eventual healing is0, prohibited, capped or unfunded. No retargeting after observing results; area spells do not harvest a separate heal from every target. The same continuing spell can qualify again in a later real round/window.

Raw self-healing is `floor(actual necrotic damage dealt /2)`. Use only the actual necrotic component, including actual temporary-HP absorption and normal HP lost under the existing actual-damage interface; no overkill. Targets must be genuine hostile opposition, not friendly/staged/trivial sacrifices or owner/ally-generated farming bodies. Natural attacks, Agony Lance and the Necrotic Affinity die alone are not spells. The feat removes no Wounds and cannot resurrect its dead owner.

**NEW finite resource — Lifeleech Recovery Reserve:** newly acquiring the feat starts at0. At each actual completed long rest set its capacity and remaining points to `2 × current character level`, snapshotted then. Level/PB changes between rests do not refill/recompute it. This reserve is neither RP nor Mutation Recovery Reserve. Persistent save imports must preserve validated spent state.

Run the ordinary two-pass healing modifiers/reductions/prohibitions. Preview uses available reserve to determine whether conditional bonuses requiring positive actual HP restoration qualify. Apply reductions before funding. Cap final legal healing potential by remaining reserve; spend that **entire funded amount** on commitment, including funded excess. All lawful healing bonuses consume this same reserve. Then restore HP subject to ordinary maximum HP and Critical ceiling, and calculate `genuine excess = max(0, funded amount − ordinary missing HP)`.

A broad HP-gain prohibition produces0 legal amount, spends0 reserve and creates0 excess. At reserve0 the round/root trigger still commits, but it produces neither restoration nor excess. Full HP can produce funded excess, but does not enable conditional bonuses requiring actual HP restoration. Critical's ceiling does not itself turn all unrestored points into excess.

Lifeleech provides no intrinsic excess converter. A separately authorized converter must have its own eligibility/cost/cadence/cap and consume each funded excess point once. An explicitly legal resource-output converter remains possible; incidental heal-triggered resource production is blocked. The child heal carries `noLifeleechRetrigger`, `blockHealCopyTriggers` and `blockResourceTriggers`; propagate these to downstream callers. The resource flag blocks incidental triggers, not an exact, separately paid excess-conversion transaction. No new resource converter is granted here.

Lifeleech also automatically collects one Soul Charge at an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, perceived with legal line of effect. No crystal is required for Lifeleech's own collection. Use the shared resource/death rules below. Lifeleech alone cannot spend charges through abilities from the unowned Soul Cage feat.

## Soul Cage feat — Magic; level8+ and (Lifeleech **or** actual spellcasting ability)

On acquisition, lock one actually possessed spellcasting source/ability as this feat's DC provider. Agony uses that source's current normal spell-save DC. No freely switchable DC ability or general retraining is created.

**Shared Soul Charges:** each owner has one persistent pool0..3, shared with Lifeleech. A charge is a soul **spark/residue**, not custody of the whole soul. It neither prevents resurrection nor replaces/removes Soul Bind. The ordinary Soul Cage spell is a separate rank6/13RP spell awaiting its own operational review. Soulrender's separate whole-soul ritual unlock still requires actually binding the soul of a living named enemy; residue cannot satisfy it.

At an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, with perception and legal line of effect, Soul Cage permits immediate optional capture with no Action or Reaction. A discrete physical black crystal must actually be possessed and available. Lifeleech collection is automatic and needs no crystal. Owning both never gives two charges for the same death.

Each owner permanently records the exact death event as evaluated, including ineligible events. There is no later corpse rescan after moving closer, gaining a feat/crystal or improving perception. For an eligible event, also reserve the immutable body for that owner's current completed-long-rest epoch. Declining or being at full capacity consumes that entitlement; there is no latent fourth charge. A new real death after resurrection is a new event, but the same body cannot supply the owner again in the same epoch. A future completed rest can permit a future new death, never the old corpse. Different owners evaluate independently.

Created/generated farming bodies and immutable object-origin transformed creatures are ineligible. Soul status otherwise follows actual source/canon or Director adjudication; this feat does not declare every undead/construct category soulless. Death/root/body identities persist through forms.

Charges live on the owner and do not decay automatically. Losing/destroying/transferring the crystal transfers or erases **zero** charges; Soul Cage capture/spending is unavailable without another actual legal black crystal. Another feat owner can use the transferred physical crystal for their own pool. There is no invented price, attunement, HP, durability or crystal charge capacity. During one uninterrupted quiet minute handling the crystal, you may voluntarily dissipate owned charges; this does nothing to any deceased soul.

**Shield:** Bonus Action; pay1 Soul Charge; one legal ally within30ft, including yourself; roll2d8 temporary HP with default lifetime. Pay before strongest-only comparison. An equal/stronger old shield does not refund the charge or Bonus Action.

**Agony Lance:** Action; pay2 Soul Charges; one perceived legal creature within60ft; CON save against the locked provider's current DC. Deal3d8 necrotic damage, half rounded down on success, then ordinary defenses/Core apply once. This is feat damage owned by you, not a spell, RP expenditure or spellcasting trigger.

The target also gains one **Agony healing-suppression family** record until the next committed ordinary HP-healing event with positive pre-reduction potential, or one elapsed minute. That next healing receives an exact×1/2 factor in the canonical healing pipeline. Save success or necrotic immunity affects damage but does not remove this separate rider. Multiple Agony Lances never multiply to1/4: a new paid application refreshes the single endpoint to `max(old expiry, new application+60s)` and retains contributor history.

Consume the suppression on the first applicable committed healing event even if a stronger arithmetic branch wins or actual healing is later capped/prohibited. Suppressed/inapplicable records do not apply or consume; absolute time continues. Temporary HP, stabilization, resurrection, prevention and maximum-HP changes are not ordinary HP healing and do not consume it. Removal requires an exact source capable of removing this magical suppression/debuff; generic cure is insufficient.

**NEW:** prerequisite parsing, residue identity, shared resource/death transaction, conduit role, activations/ranges/DC and the exact healing-suppression conversion. Original source IDs and relationships remain distinct.

# Shared rules for the class playtest drafts

**Provisional design integration, 8 October 2026.** These rules make the class drafts usable together for testing. They preserve each protected class engine while specifying missing timing and replacing conflicting old percentages. They do not rewrite the approved Word books. Original descriptions and alternate registry entries remain in `data/playtest/class_sources`.

## Reading a class card

Use the class's own level, never total character level, for gates and effects. **L** means that class level; **S** is 1/2/3/4 at class levels 1/5/11/17. **M** means max(1, the class ability modifier), for effect a mounts only. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. Negative modifiers still apply to attacks and DCs. One tile is 5 ft. Fractions round down unless specified. Distances cannot be negative.

A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one.

An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

## Action and timing limits

One regular Action, one Bonus Action if a feature permits it, normal movement and one Reaction between starts of your turns. A free trigger costs no Action only if expressly stated. All grants share **one extra full Action per creature per round**. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. A card granting additional attacks is not permission to repeat all class riders on every hit: obey each rider's frequency.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.

## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.

## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.

## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.

Generic Overcast is excluded from the initial suite configuration until its options are separately fixed; cards such as Overchannel have their own exact costs and gates. Core V 2's original Burn procedures, older rank×2 costs and smaller companion RP tables remain preserved as alternatives, not silently combined. This configuration is suit able for comparing class drafts, not a claim that all historical magic sources already agree.

## Spell repertoires and acquisition

Preserve explicit class spellbook/preparation rules where given. For classes missing a known-spell count, this suite proposes: full casters know 3 cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10 and choose 2 ranked spells at first spell access plus 1 each later class level; hybrid/half/minor casters know 2 cantrips at first cantrip access and 3 at class 10, and choose 2 ranked spells at first ranked access plus 1 on each later even class level. At a long rest, a known caster may replace one known spell with a legal same-or-lower rank selection. This fills an actual missing rule and does not replace a more specific Druid prepared list or Wizard spellbook. Bonus spells expressly granted by a class are additional. No unnamed or mechanically unfinished catalog spell becomes complete merely by entering this repertoire; select operational spells for the test and record them.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.

Earlier contradictory level-table entries are retained as source evidence and marked reconciled/replaced for this draft; never stack them on top of the new schedule. ## Core condition reference

The following descriptions are preserved from [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../data/public/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Data_v2_Known_Descent.json). The class suite adds its explicit duration, escape and hard-denial limits; it does not give the same named condition a different meaning in each class. Dread, Grief, Bleed and other custom riders use their card’s exact definition.

| Condition | Core V2 rule |
|---|---|
| Blinded | Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. |
| Charmed | Cannot willingly harm the charmer; charmer has advantage on social checks against it. |
| Deafened | Cannot hear and fails hearing checks; verbal coordination may fail. |
| Frightened | Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. |
| Grappled | Speed 0; ends if grappler is incapacitated or reach is broken. |
| Incapacitated | Cannot take actions or reactions. |
| Invisible | Cannot be seen normally; attacks against it have disadvantage and its attacks have advantage until location is revealed. |
| Paralyzed | Incapacitated, cannot move or speak, fails Strength/Dexterity saves, adjacent hits are critical. |
| Poisoned | Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks. |
| Prone | Crawl or stand; melee attackers within 5 ft. have advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage. |
| Restrained | Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. |
| Silenced | Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. |
| Staggered | Cannot react, loses Guard, and the next forced movement gains +5 ft. Ends at start of next turn. |
| Stunned | Incapacitated, cannot move, fails Strength/Dexterity saves, attacks against have advantage. |
| Unconscious | Incapacitated, unaware, drops held items, falls Prone, adjacent hits are critical. |
